This project demonstrates the design and generation of a realistic procurement dataset covering supplier management, sourcing, purchasing, invoicing, and supplier performance evaluation. The dataset was developed for procurement analytics, dashboard development, machine learning, and training purposes.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

### Introduction
Procurement functions generate large volumes of operational and financial data that can be leveraged to improve sourcing decisions, supplier performance, spend visibility, and organizational efficiency. However, access to real procurement datasets is often constrained by confidentiality, privacy, and commercial sensitivity.

This project presents a synthetic procurement dataset designed to simulate the end-to-end procurement lifecycle of a medium-to-large enterprise. The dataset was developed for analytics training, dashboard development, data modeling, machine learning experimentation, and procurement performance analysis. While the data is artificially generated, the business relationships and procurement workflows have been structured to closely resemble real-world procurement operations.

The business linkage models actual business process flow:
Supplier → Product → Price → Purchase Requisition → Purchase Order → Invoice → Supplier Performance Analysis.

### Business Objective
The primary objective of this project is to create a realistic procurement dataset that enables analysts, students, and professionals to develop practical skills in procurement and supply chain analytics.

The dataset supports the analysis of key procurement activities including:

- Supplier management
- Purchase requisitions
- Purchase orders
- Invoice processing
- Vendor performance monitoring
- Procurement risk management
- Spend analysis
- Operational efficiency measurement

### Dataset Overview
This synthetic dataset simulates the end-to-end procurement lifecycle of a medium-to-large enterprise operating across multiple departments and supplier categories. It provides a robust foundation for:

- Advanced procurement analytics
- Spend and cost optimization analysis
- Supplier performance and risk assessment
- Executive dashboards and operational reporting
- Predictive modeling and forecasting
- Machine learning and artificial intelligence applications
- Procurement process improvement and efficiency analysis
- Supplier segmentation and strategic sourcing analysis
- Procurement KPI tracking and performance measurement
- Training, simulation, and analytics education

The dataset contains:

 - 100 suppliers
 - 39 products and services
 - 3,000 purchase requisitions
 - Purchase orders generated from approved requisitions
 - Supplier invoices
 - Supplier performance metrics

The procurement ecosystem consists of:

##### Master Data

 - Product Master
 - Supplier Master
 - Product Pricing Catalog

##### Transactional Data

 - Purchase Requisitions (PR)
 - Purchase Orders (PO)
 - Supplier Invoices

##### Analytical Data

 - Supplier Risk Assessment
 - Supplier Satisfaction Metrics
 - Delivery Performance Metrics
 - Supplier Segmentation

The dataset includes procurement activities across multiple departments such as Finance, Supply Chain, Procurement, IT, Legal, Sustainability, Human Resources, Sales, Marketing, Engineering, and Risk Management

### Dataset Structure
The project consists of the following datasets:

#### 1. Product Master
Contains information on goods and services available for procurement. Key attributes include:

- Product ID
- Product Name
- Product Category
- Product Type

#### 2. Supplier Master
Contains supplier profile information. Key attributes include:

- Supplier ID
- Supplier Name
- Supplier Origin
- Supplier Classification
- Supplier Category
- Supplier Tier

#### 3. Product Price Catalog
Contains product pricing information and price ranges. Key attributes include:

- Product ID
- Price ID
- Unit Price
- Minimum Price
- Maximum Price

#### 4. Purchase Requisition
Captures procurement requests initiated by employees.

#### 5. Purchase Order
Captures approved procurement requests that have been converted into supplier orders.

#### 6. Invoice
Captures supplier billing information associated with purchase orders.

#### 7. Supplier Performance
Contains operational and satisfaction measures used for supplier evaluation.

### Potential Analytics Use Cases
The dataset can be used to answer a wide variety of procurement and supply chain business questions.

#### Spend Analytics

- Who are the highest-spend suppliers?
- Which categories account for the largest procurement spend?
- What departments generate the highest purchasing activity?

#### Supplier Analytics

- Which suppliers present the highest operational risk?
- How does supplier performance vary by category?
- What percentage of spending goes to strategic suppliers?

#### Operational Analytics

- What is the average procurement cycle time?
- Which departments experience the longest approval delays?
- What proportion of orders are delivered on time?

#### Procurement Performance Dashboards

- Supplier scorecards
- Spend dashboards
- Purchase order tracking
- Delivery performance monitoring
- Risk management dashboards

### Machine Learning Applications
Because the dataset contains structured procurement relationships, it is suitable for several machine learning use cases.

#### Classification Models

Predict:

- Purchase requisition approval
- Purchase order status
- On-time delivery
- Supplier risk classification

#### Regression Models

Predict:

- Cycle time
- Procurement spend
- Supplier satisfaction scores
- Delivery lead time

#### Clustering

Segment suppliers by:

- Risk
- Spend
- Strategic importance
- Satisfaction levels

#### Anomaly Detection

Identify:

- Unusual purchase behavior
- Low-performing suppliers
- Abnormal transaction patterns
- Potential procurement control violations

### Dataset Generation Methodology
The dataset was generated using a rule-based synthetic data generation approach implemented in R.
The methodology consisted of the following steps:

1.	Creation of product master records containing goods and service categories.
2.	Generation of realistic product price ranges.
3.	Creation of supplier master records with tiering, classifications, and segmentation attributes.
4.	Mapping suppliers to products and services.
5.	Generating purchase requisitions from departmental demand.
6.	Converting approved requisitions into purchase orders.
7.	Generating invoices from purchase orders.
8.	Calculating supplier performance metrics including risk, impact, satisfaction, and delivery indicators.

Randomization techniques were combined with predefined business rules to simulate realistic procurement scenarios while preserving logical relationships across datasets.

### Appendix A: Dataset Generation Code
The complete R code used to generate the synthetic dataset is provided in this appendix.

The code demonstrates:

- Synthetic master-data creation
- Procurement transaction simulation
- Business-rule implementation
- Data relationships and joins
- Supplier scorecard generation
- Performance metric calculation

Users can modify the parameters, probabilities, categories, and business rules to generate alternative procurement scenarios for analytics training and experimentation.

```{r libraries, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)

```


#### Define Key Reference Data for Procurement Dataset Generation
This synthetic procurement dataset was generated using predefined reference data covering employees, departments, suppliers, procurement categories, and sourcing characteristics. Details are provided below.
```{r procurement_dataset, echo=FALSE}

set.seed(911)
# requester info
fname = c("Kwasi" ,"Kojo" ,"Kwabena" ,"Kwaku" ,"Yaw" ,"Kofi" ,"Kwame" ,
          "Akosua" ,"Adjoa" ,"Abena" ,"Akua" ,"Yaa" ,"Efia" ,"Ama")
lname = c("Adams" ,"Adjei" ,"Bill" ,"Boakye" ,"Doe" ,"Fosu" ,"Mensah" ,
          "Ntim" ,"Odum" ,"Okine" ,"Opoku" ,"Osei" ,"Owusu" ,"Smith")
department = c("finance", "legal", "sustainability", "HR", "supply chain", "operations", "procurement",
               "risk management" ,"sales" ,"marketing" ,"IT" ,"engineering")

# Supplier details
supplier_ID = sprintf("SUP%03d", 1:100)
supplier_nm = paste0("supplier " ,sample(LETTERS ,100 ,replace = TRUE) ,supplier_ID)
supplier_origin = c(rep("local", 85) ,rep("international", 15) )
supplier_category = sample(c("strategic" ,"preferred" ,"tactical" ,"bottleneck" ,"nuisance") ,
                           prob = c(0.4 ,0.3 ,0.2 ,0.06 ,0.04) ,100 ,replace = TRUE)
tier = sample(c(1:3) ,prob = c(0.5 ,0.3 ,0.2) ,100 ,replace = TRUE)
classification = sample(c("contractor" ,"OEM" ,"service provider") ,
                        prob = c(0.7 ,0.2 ,0.1) ,100 ,replace = TRUE)

# product details
product_services = c("calibration" ,"catering" ,"consulting" ,"construction" ,
                     "equipment maintenance"  ,"facility maintenance" ,"IT systems" ,
                     "logistics" ,"research" ,
                     "security" ,"shipping" ,"storage" ,"training" ,"waste management") 
product_goods_office = c("furniture"  ,"lighting fixtures" ,"stationery" ,"toiletries") 
product_goods_agric = c("canola" ,"coconut" ,"corn" ,
                        "olive" ,"palm", "palm kernel",
                        "rapeseed" ,"rice" ,
                        "shea" ,"sorghum"  ,"soybeans" ,"sunflower" , 
                        "wheat"  ,"herbicides", "pesticides")
product_goods_misc = c("labels" ,"packaging materials" ,"premix" ,"rentals" ,"spare parts"  ,"water")

# tag = sample("logistics" ,"IT hardware" ,"consulting" ,"training" ,"fuel" ,"water")

# average price range
price_range = c("850-1200" ,"1200-1600" ,"850-1200" ,"65-120" ,"700-1100" ,"700-1100" ,"850-1200" ,
                "850-1200" ,"35-50" ,"850-1200" ,"850-1200" ,"850-1200" ,"850-1200" ,"45-90" ,
                "45-90" ,"0.30-3.50" ,"0.40-2.50" ,"35-50" ,"1700-3800" ,"100-2000" ,"2-10" ,
                "1450-2530" ,"13-1500" ,"4-50" ,"20-150" ,"600-2500" ,"30-400" ,"5500-6500" ,
                "80-95" ,"100-400" ,"150-800" ,"500-1500" ,"600-2000" ,"65000-850000" ,
                "1200-6000" ,"2500-10000" ,"9500-25000" ,"1500-7000" ,"30-50") 

# dates for PR and PO
date_from = as.Date("2025-01-01")
date_to = as.Date("2026-09-28")
date = seq.Date(date_from ,date_to ,"day")

delivery_eta = c(30 ,60 ,90 ,180)
delivery_otd = seq(20, 190, by = 10)

# List of licensed banks in Ghana (2026)
bank_name = c("Absa Bank" ,"Access Bank" ,"ADB" ,"Bank of Africa" ,"CalBank" ,"CBG" ,"Ecobank" ,"FirstBank" ,
              "Fidelity Bank" ,"First Atlantic" ,"First National Bank" ,"GCB" ,"GTBank" ,"NIB" ,
              "OmniBSIC" ,"Prudential" ,"Republic Bank" ,"Stanbic" ,"StanChart" ,"UBA" ,"UMB" ,"Zenith")
bank_branch = c("Tema" ,"Ashiaman" ,"Accra" ,"Kumasi" ,"Takoradi" ,"Sunyani" ,"Osu" ,"Koforidua" ,
                "Cape Coast" ,"Techiman" ,"Ho" ,"Kpando" ,"Wiawso" ,"Tarkwa" ,"Suhum" ,"Hohoe")

```

#### 1. Create master product reference table for goods and services
```{r master data, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
product_details = rbind(data.frame(product_type = "goods" ,
                                   product_category = "agriculture" ,
                                   product_name = product_goods_agric ) ,
                        data.frame(product_type = "goods" ,
                                   product_category = "miscellaneous" ,
                                   product_name  = product_goods_misc) ,
                        data.frame(product_type = "goods" ,
                                   product_category = "office supplies" ,
                                   product_name  = product_goods_office) ,
                        data.frame(product_type = "services" ,
                                   product_category = "service" ,
                                   product_name  = product_services)  ) %>%
  mutate(product_id = sprintf("PROD%03d" ,1:39) ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(1:4) ,as.factor) ,
         freq = 1)

```

#### 2. Generate Product Price Ranges
```{r product price list, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# Average Prices in Ghana (2026) with Product IDs

set.seed(911)
price_list = bind_rows(replicate(5 ,
                    data.frame(product_id = sprintf("PROD%03d" ,1:39) ,
                               price_range = price_range) %>%
                      
                      left_join(data.frame(product_id = product_details[,4] ,
                                           product_name = product_details[,3] ) )  %>%
                      separate(price_range, into = c("min_price", "max_price"), sep = "-") %>%
                      mutate(across(c("min_price", "max_price") ,as.numeric)) ,
                    simplify = FALSE)) %>%
   mutate(price = round(rnorm(n() ,
                       mean = (max_price + min_price)/2 ,
                       sd = (max_price - min_price)/6) ,2) ) %>%
  mutate(price_id = sprintf("PRID%003d" ,1:n()) ,
         freq = 1) %>%
  select(-min_price ,-max_price)

```

#### 3. Supplier Information
```{r supplier, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
set.seed(911)
suppliers = data.frame(supplier_ID = supplier_ID ,
                       supplier_name = supplier_nm ,
                       supplier_origin = supplier_origin ,
                       supplier_category = supplier_category ,
                       tier = tier ,
                       classification = classification ,
                       demographics = "" ,freq = 1) %>%
  mutate(bank_info = paste(sample(bank_name ,100 ,replace = TRUE) ,"-" ,
                            sample(bank_branch ,100 ,replace = TRUE) )) %>%
  mutate(across(c(1:4,6,7,9) ,as.factor))

```

#### 4a. supplier product map function
```{r supplier product, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
supplier_product = lapply(suppliers[,1] ,function(s){
  data.frame(supplier = s ,
   product = as.factor(sample(product_details[,4] ,5)) ,
   freq = 1)
  } ) %>%
  
  do.call(rbind,.)

```

#### 4b. supplier product map data
```{r supplier product mapping, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
supplier_prodDetails = supplier_product %>%
  left_join(suppliers ,by = c("supplier" = "supplier_ID") ,suffix = c(x="" ,y="")) %>%
  left_join(product_details ,by = c("product" = "product_id") ,suffix = c(x="" ,y="")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(2,11,12,13) ,as.factor))

```

#### 4c. supplier price list
```{r pricelist, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
supplier_price_list = supplier_prodDetails %>%
  left_join(price_list ,by = c("product" = "product_id") ,suffix = c(x="" ,y=""))

```

#### 5. Purchase Requisition
```{r PR, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
set.seed(123)
product_request = supplier_price_list %>%
  slice(rep(1:n() ,length.out=3000))

purchase_requisition = data.frame(pr_number = sprintf("PR%04d" ,1:3000) ,
                                  requester = paste(sample(fname ,3000 ,replace = TRUE) ,
                                                    sample(lname ,3000 ,replace = TRUE)) ,
                                  department = sample(department ,3000 ,replace = TRUE) ,
                                  product_type = product_request[,11]   ,
                                  product_category = product_request[,12]  ,
                                  product_name = product_request[,13]  ,
                                  product_id = product_request[,2]  ,
                                  description = "" ,
                                  UoM = as.factor("") ,
                                  quantity = round(rnorm(3000 ,400 ,100) ,0)  ,
                                  unit_price = product_request[,14] ,
                                  prefered_supplier = product_request[,1] ,
                                  date_requested = sample(date ,3000 ,replace = TRUE) - 30 ) %>%
  mutate(quantity = ifelse(product_category == "service" ,round(quantity/100,0) ,round(quantity/10,0)) ,
         date_expected = date_requested + round(rnorm(3000 ,45 ,10) ,0) ,
         contact = paste0(requester ,"@bunge.com") ,
         pr_approval = sample(c("yes" ,"no") ,prob = c(0.9 ,0.1) ,3000 ,replace = TRUE) ,
         freq = 1 ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(1:4,7,8,15,16) ,as.factor))

```

#### 6. Purchase Order after approval of request
```{r PO, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
set.seed(911)
len_po = length(purchase_requisition$pr_approval[purchase_requisition$pr_approval == "yes"])

purchase_order = purchase_requisition %>%
  filter(pr_approval == "yes") %>%
  mutate(total_price = unit_price * quantity ,
         #invoiced = sample(c("yes" ,"no") ,prob = c(0.95 ,0.05) ,len_po ,replace = TRUE) ,
         PO_number = as.factor(paste0(year(date_requested) ,"-" ,sprintf("%05d" ,seq(c(1:len_po))))) ,
         date_order = date_requested + sample(7:14 ,len_po ,replace = TRUE) ,
         eta = sample(delivery_eta ,prob = c(0.6 ,0.2 ,0.15 ,0.05) ,len_po ,replace = TRUE) ,
         cycling_time = round(rnorm(len_po ,110 ,30) ,0) ,
           #sample(delivery_otd ,prob = c(0.4, rep(0.6/17, 17)) ,len_po ,replace = TRUE) ,
         supplier_ID = prefered_supplier ,
         status = as.factor(sample(c("sent" ,"pending") ,len_po ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.95 ,0.05))) ) %>%
  mutate(status = as.factor(ifelse(status == "sent" & product_name == "research" ,"pending" ,
                                   paste(status))) ,
         date_order = case_when(status == "sent" ~ date_order ,status == "pending" ~ as.Date(0)) ,
         eta = as.numeric(ifelse(status == "sent" ,eta ,"")) ,
         cycling_time = as.numeric(ifelse(eta == 30 ,round(rnorm(1000 ,30 ,5) ,0) ,
                                          ifelse(status == "sent" ,cycling_time ,""))) )%>%
  mutate(total_price = as.numeric(ifelse(status == "sent" ,unit_price * quantity ,"")) ) %>%
  select(-c(2:5, 14:15))

```

#### 7. Invoice while process order
```{r invoice, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
set.seed(911)
len_invoice = length(purchase_order$status[purchase_order$status == "sent"])

invoice = suppliers %>%
  select(supplier_ID ,supplier_name ,bank_info) %>%
  
  left_join(
  purchase_order %>%
  filter(status == "sent") %>%
  mutate(total_price = unit_price * quantity ,
         invoice_no = sample(sprintf("INV%04d" ,1:len_invoice) ,len_invoice ,replace = TRUE) ,
         PO_number = paste0(year(date_requested) ,"-" ,sprintf("%05d" ,seq(c(1:len_invoice)))) ,
         date_order = date_requested + sample(7:14 ,len_invoice ,replace = TRUE) ,
         eta = sample(c(30 ,60 ,90 ,180) ,prob = c(0.6 ,0.2 ,0.15 ,0.05) ,len_invoice ,replace = TRUE) ,
         otd = sample(seq(20, 190, by = 10) ,len_invoice ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.4, rep(0.6/17, 17))) )         ,by = c("supplier_ID" = "prefered_supplier") ,suffix = c(x="" ,y="") ) %>%
  mutate(invoice_no = paste0(word(supplier_name ,2) ,"-" ,invoice_no) ) %>%
  select(-c(4,10,17)) %>% mutate(across(c(13,18) ,as.factor))

```

#### 8. supplier analysis
```{r supplier analytics, echo=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
set.seed(911)
len_sup = nrow(purchase_order)


supplier_analysis = suppliers %>%
  mutate(risk = sample(1:5 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.35 ,0.30 ,0.20 ,0.10 ,0.05) ) ,
         impact = sample(1:5 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.10 ,0.10 ,0.30 ,0.20 ,0.30) ) ,
         psat = sample(1:5 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.10,0.10,0.2,0.3,0.3))  ,
         csat = sample(1:5 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.15,0.15,0.1,0.3,0.3)) ,
          nps = sample(0:10 ,100 ,replace = TRUE ,
                        prob = c(0.04,0.04, 0.04, 0.04, 0.04, 0.04 ,0.04,
                                 0.21 ,0.11 ,
                                 0.20 ,0.20))  ) %>%
  mutate(nps_cat = ifelse(nps > 8 ,"promoter" ,ifelse(nps < 7 ,"detractor" ,
                   ifelse(nps %in% c(7,8) ,"passive" ,nps))) ,
         psat_cat = ifelse(psat > 3,"high" ,ifelse(psat < 3,"low" ,ifelse(psat == 3,"medium" ,psat))) ,
         csat_cat = ifelse(csat > 3,"high" ,ifelse(csat < 3,"low" ,ifelse(csat == 3,"medium" ,csat))) ,
         risk_level = ifelse(risk > 3,"high" ,ifelse(risk < 3,"low" ,ifelse(risk == 3,"medium" ,csat))) ,
         impact_level = ifelse(impact > 3,"high" ,ifelse(impact < 3,"low" ,
                      ifelse(impact == 3,"medium" ,csat)))) %>%
  
  right_join(purchase_order) %>%
  left_join(product_details ,suffix = c(x="" ,y="") ) %>%
  
  mutate(status_delivery = ifelse(eta >= cycling_time ,"on-time" ,"delayed") ,
         defects = ifelse(status == "sent" & product_type == "goods" ,
                          sample(c("no" ,"yes") ,len_sup ,replace = TRUE ,prob = c(0.8,0.2)) ,"" )) %>%
  mutate(across(c(15:19,24,29,38,39) ,as.factor))

```
